Compute Centrality Measures for a Network

Source: R/centrality_measures.R
net_centrality.Rd

net_centrality() scores how central each node is in a network, for one or more measures, and returns one row per node. Strength sums a node's edge weights (incoming or outgoing); closeness and betweenness read the shortest paths between nodes, where a heavier edge is a shorter step; diffusion counts the weighted walks that start at a node; and clustering measures how strongly a node's neighbours are tied to each other. It takes a single network or a group of them (a netobject_group, the clusters of an mcml), scoring each separately.

Centralities describe the estimated network, not the population it was estimated from. Rankings built on a few weak edges change from sample to sample: check them with centrality_stability() before reporting which node is most central.

Usage

net_centrality(
  x,
  measures = NULL,
  loops = FALSE,
  normalize = FALSE,
  invert = TRUE,
  normalize_diffusion = TRUE,
  centrality_fn = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'net_centrality'
plot(
  x,
  reorder = TRUE,
  ncol = 3L,
  type = c("bar", "line", "heatmap"),
  scales = c("free_x", "fixed"),
  profile_scale = c("measure", "none"),
  labels = TRUE,
  drop_zero = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'net_centrality_group'
plot(
  x,
  reorder = TRUE,
  ncol = 3L,
  type = c("bar", "line", "delta"),
  scales = c("free_x", "fixed"),
  palette = "Set2",
  profile_scale = c("measure", "none"),
  labels = FALSE,
  drop_zero = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

The network: a netobject, netobject_group, mcml or cograph_network. For the plot() methods: the result of net_centrality().

measures

The measures to compute. The default is "InStrength", "Betweenness" and "Diffusion"; "all" computes every built-in one: "OutStrength" and "InStrength" (sum of outgoing or incoming weights), "ClosenessOut", "ClosenessIn" and "Closeness" (inverse of the summed shortest-path distances from, to, or ignoring the direction of edges), "Betweenness" (how many shortest paths pass through the node), "BetweennessRSP" (betweenness over randomised shortest paths, which also counts near-shortest routes), "Diffusion" (the summed weights of walks of length 1 to n from the node) and "Clustering" (weighted clustering coefficient). "InCloseness" and "OutCloseness" are accepted for "ClosenessIn" and "ClosenessOut". With centrality_fn, name its measures here to have them returned.

loops

Whether self-loops (staying in a state) count. With FALSE (default) they are left out of every measure, and a message says so.

normalize

Whether to range-normalise every measure to 0–1, as tna::centralities(normalize = TRUE) does. Default FALSE.

invert

Whether a heavier edge is a shorter step in the shortest-path measures (distance = 1 / weight), as in tna. With FALSE, the weight itself is the distance. Default TRUE.

normalize_diffusion

Whether to range-normalise Diffusion even when normalize = FALSE. Default TRUE.

centrality_fn

A function of your own that takes the weight matrix and returns a named list of centrality vectors, one per measure; list their names in measures. Default NULL.

...

Not used.

reorder

For the plot() methods: whether to sort the nodes in each measure's panel by their value (for a group, by their mean value across networks). Default TRUE.

ncol

For the plot() methods: the number of panel columns. Default 3.

type

For the plot() methods: the kind of plot. "bar" (default) draws one panel of bars per measure, grouped bars for several networks. "line" draws each node's profile across the measures (for several networks, one panel per node and one line per network); "profile" is accepted for it. A single network also takes "heatmap", a nodes-by-measures grid with each measure scaled to 0–1 for the colour and its raw value printed in the tile. Several networks also take "delta", bars of the differences between networks: the second minus the first with two, each network's deviation from the per-node mean with more.

scales

For the plot() methods: "free_x" (default) gives each measure its own value axis, "fixed" one shared axis.

profile_scale

For type = "line": "measure" (default) rescales each measure to 0–1 so the profiles compare across measures; "none" draws raw values.

labels

For the plot() methods: whether to print the values on the plot. Default TRUE for one network, FALSE for several.

drop_zero

For the plot() methods: whether to leave out measures that are zero for every node. Default FALSE.

palette

For plot() of several networks: the ColorBrewer palette for the networks. Default "Set2". Ignored by type = "delta" with two networks, whose bars are coloured by which network is higher.

Value

For a netobject or cograph_network: a net_centrality data frame with one row per node, a state column and one column per requested measure (the node names are also the row names). For a netobject_group or an mcml: a net_centrality_group, a list of such data frames, one per network. plot() draws the measures per node.

For the plot() methods: a ggplot object.

Details

Strength is read from the weight matrix directly, and closeness and betweenness from all-pairs shortest paths (Floyd-Warshall), without igraph; the values agree with tna::centralities(). Diffusion is range-normalised by default, which tna does not do.

Range normalisation of a measure that is the same for every node is undefined and gives NaN, with a warning of class nestimate_constant_measure. Diffusion on a "relative" network with loops = TRUE is such a case: each row sums to 1, so every node has the same diffusion; use normalize_diffusion = FALSE there.

References

Freeman, L. C. (1978). Centrality in social networks: conceptual clarification. Social Networks, 1(3), 215–239. (betweenness, closeness)

Opsahl, T., Agneessens, F. & Skvoretz, J. (2010). Node centrality in weighted networks: generalizing degree and shortest paths. Social Networks, 32(3), 245–251. (weighted strength and geodesics)

Kivimaki, I., Lebichot, B., Saramaki, J. & Saerens, M. (2016). Two betweenness centrality measures based on randomized shortest paths. Scientific Reports, 6, 19668. (BetweennessRSP)

Banerjee, A., Chandrasekhar, A. G., Duflo, E. & Jackson, M. O. (2013). The diffusion of microfinance. Science, 341(6144), 1236498. (Diffusion)

Onnela, J.-P., Saramaki, J., Kertesz, J. & Kaski, K. (2005). Intensity and coherence of motifs in weighted complex networks. Physical Review E, 71, 065103. (Clustering)

Examples

seqs <- data.frame(
  V1 = c("A","B","A","C"), V2 = c("B","C","B","A"),
  V3 = c("C","A","C","B"))
net <- build_network(seqs, method = "relative")
net_centrality(net)
#> centralities computed excluding loops (diagonal). Pass `loops = TRUE` to include self-transitions.
#> Warning: Diffusion is the same for every node, so it cannot be range-normalised and is NaN. Use `normalize_diffusion = FALSE` for the raw values.
#>   state InStrength Betweenness Diffusion
#> A     A          1           1       NaN
#> B     B          1           1       NaN
#> C     C          1           1       NaN
